In algebra, a '''Taft Hopf algebra''' is a [[Hopf algebra]]  introduced by {{harvs|first=Earl|last=Taft|authorlink=Earl Taft|year=1971|txt}} that is neither [[commutative]] nor [[cocommutative]] and has an [[Antipode (algebra)|antipode]] of large even order.

==Construction==

Suppose that ''k'' is a [[Field (algebra)|field]] with a primitive ''n'''th [[root of unity]] ζ for some positive integer ''n''. The Taft algebra is the ''n''<sup>2</sup>-dimensional [[associative algebra]] generated over ''k'' by ''c'' and ''x'' with the relations ''c''<sup>''n''</sup>=1, ''x''<sup>''n''</sup>=0, ''xc''=ζ''cx''. The coproduct takes ''c'' to ''c''⊗''c'' and ''x'' to ''c''⊗''x'' + ''x''⊗1.
The counit takes ''c'' to 1 and ''x'' to 0. The antipode takes ''c'' to ''c''<sup>−1</sup> and ''x'' to –''c''<sup>−1</sup>''x'': the order of the antipode is 2''n'' (if ''n'' > 1).
